checks.claim: OC1: the square map f->f^2 is a well-defined continuous map from full real H1 into the completed H_sp, with pairings equal to the physical B.
checks.reason: For smooth compact f_n->f in H1, ||f_n^2-f_m^2||^2=C4(f_n-f_m,f_n+f_m,f_n-f_m,f_n+f_m)<=R0 N(f_n-f_m)^2 N(f_n+f_m)^2 by bridge (15), so the squares are Cauchy. Joint continuity of C4 gives independence of the sequence, the norm B(f^2,f^2), the pairing B(f^2,h^2) and continuity of the map. No H1-Linfinity embedding or d1 split is needed, so the route is valid in d2/3 for singular and invariant-direction Gamma.

checks.claim: OC1: for g in O, rho_g is strongly measurable and in L2(I;H_sp), and its PB0 image in H_I has squared norm exactly A(g).
checks.reason: Strong measurability follows by composing a continuous map with a separably valued strongly measurable field. ||g_s^2||^2=A_sp(g_s)<=R_sp b_s^(alpha/2), which is integrable since alpha<2 and b is integrable. PB (20) extends the bilinear identity to all of L2(I;G), with <F(s),F(t)>=B(g_s^2,g_t^2) a.e. Hence the norm is the physical raw-K integral, not an abstract covariance or the damped K_star.

checks.claim: OC1: K0=2^a/(1-a) and 0<=A(g)<=K0 R_sp T(g)^(alpha/2), with T(g)>0 and 0<C_occ<=K0 R_sp.
checks.reason: The raw row is [s^(1-a)+(1-s)^(1-a)]/(1-a), with maximum 2^a/(1-a) at s=1/2. Bridge (11),(16) gives B<=R_sp F(s)F(t) with F=b^(alpha/4). Symmetric Schur gives K0 int b^(alpha/2), and concavity on the unit interval gives K0 T^(alpha/2). T>0 because a unit L2 function has nonzero weak gradient. A constant-time unit compact bump gives positive C_occ using bridge A_sp>0.

checks.reason: U_ell scales B by ell^(2d-d+alpha-d)=ell^alpha through Radon pushforward and scales T by ell^2. It is an L2-unitary H1 bijection on O with inverse U_(1/ell). Maximizing ell^alpha A-eta ell^2 T gives (2-alpha)/2*(alpha/(2eta))^(alpha/(2-alpha))*(A/T^(alpha/2))^(2/(2-alpha)), which I rederived. Approximating C_occ from below gives the reverse inequality without an optimizer. Any g with A=0 has negative score and cannot affect the positive supremum.

checks.claim: OC2: the countable first-index near-selector is well defined, measurable, strongly H1 and in O.
checks.reason: Normalizing a countable H1-dense subset of C_c^infinity gives a family dense in the L2-unit H1 sphere. UL (9),(11),(12) make the form s->int h_s f_j^2-||grad f_j||^2 and lambda continuous on I, so the cells are open and cover I. int h f_j^2-b_j>lambda^2-eps with lambda^2>=0 and unit mass gives b_j<H+eps, so T is finite. No unmasked eigenfunction or continuum selector is used, which also covers invariant-direction Gamma where the bottom need not be an eigenvalue.

All steps fit the stated guards, and neither equality nor the reverse inequality is required.

minor: The eta=1 negative sign is structural for alpha>=1, not a feature of sampled rows. Delta increases in a, and on a<2-alpha its supremum is [(4-alpha)log(4-alpha)+alpha log alpha]/2-2log2, which decreases in alpha and is about 0.2616 at alpha=1. Since (alpha/2)log2>=0.3466, the sign is strictly negative throughout the admissible alpha>=1 range, including every d2/3 alpha>1 model. The four negative screen rows therefore reflect one analytic fact. The target's sign gate remains correct, but a favorable kinetic-1 comparison is possible only for alpha<1. This concerns bounds only, not moments.
